author: Pallas, 1776
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수백 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록
summary: 도시 공원과 정원, 교외의 큰 고목, 성긴 숲 등에 사는 여름철새로, 우리나라에서 번식하고 중국 남부와 동남아시아에서 겨울을 난다. 번식기에는 암수가 함께 지내다가 번식 뒤에는 큰 무리를 짓는다. 아주 엉성한 접시 모양 둥지를 짓고 5월 하순에 알을 3~8개 낳는다. 어미는 딱총나무, 뽕나무, 벚나무 등의 열매와 딱정벌레, 파리, 나비 애벌레 등을 즐겨 먹는다.

art.subject: Daurian Starling (Sturnus sturninus), adult male in breeding plumage (May–July in Korea): forehead, crown, face and hindneck pale ash-grey with a large glossy blackish-purple patch on the hindcrown and nape; ear coverts grey; chin and upper throat brownish-grey; breast and flanks pale grey, belly whitish; mantle and back glossy purple-black; wings glossy greenish-black with a bold white stripe along the scapulars; tail black with a green gloss; short, straight, pointed black bill; dark eye; dark grey-brown legs.
art.pose: perched in a mulberry tree, picking berries
art.scene: Korean early-summer park with large old trees and open woodland; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view perched on a branch: pale grey head and underparts, large glossy blackish-purple patch on the hindcrown, glossy purple-black back, green-black wings with a bold white scapular stripe, short black bill, dark grey-brown legs
adult male, head close-up in profile: smooth rounded pale grey head with the dark purple nape patch, grey ear coverts, brownish-grey chin and upper throat, short straight black bill, dark eye
adult female, side view perched: grey-brown head and back without gloss and without the purple nape patch, dark brown wings with a whitish scapular stripe, pale grey-white underparts
art.build: Small, compact starling, 18cm, clearly smaller and slimmer than White-cheeked Starling (Spodiopsar cineraceus), between a sparrow and a Brown-eared Bulbul in size. Typical starling shape: short square tail, pointed wings, short neck; perches upright in tree crowns. Head smooth and rounded, without a crest. Bill black, straight and pointed, shorter than the head and short for a starling. Legs medium length, dark grey-brown. In flight the triangular wings show the white scapular stripe against the dark back.
avoid: Do not give it a crest or spiky nape plumes; the head is smooth and rounded, marked only by the dark purple nape patch.
Do not paint a black head with white cheeks or an orange bill — that is White-cheeked Starling (Spodiopsar cineraceus).
Do not paint a creamy head with chestnut cheeks — that is Chestnut-cheeked Starling (Agropsar philippensis).
Do not make the bill yellow or long; it is short, straight and black.
